samples.summary: The tint regression is never exercised through DocCanvas — the test re-implements the render loop, so re-introducing the rounding bug would not fail anything
samples.evidence: The defect this diff fixes lives at doc-canvas.ts:600-611: the overlap must be tested on the *unrounded* box while only the fill rounds. `imageIntersectsSelection` itself is a plain, unconditional rectangle test — it cannot express the bug. The new test's `tintedIndicesFor` (image-selection-tint.test.ts:87-105) copies the render loop into the test file and always passes an unrounded box (`x: pageX + pl.x + run.x`), so if someone restored `Math.round(...)` at the real call site in `DocCanvas.render`, every test here still passes. Nothing in packages/docs/test drives `DocCanvas.render` with images + selectionRects and asserts the tint fillRect (grep for fillRect/DocCanvas: image-selection-overlay.test.ts records ctx.fillRect for handles only, and paint-layout/table-renderer tests do not cover this branch). The recording-ctx pattern already in image-selection-overlay.test.ts shows this is testable end-to-end. Failure mode if it regresses: a neighbouring image is wrongly tinted blue on selection (user-visible rendering artefact) with a green suite.

samples.summary: The test's copy of the render loop drops `pageY`, so its boxes are in a different vertical frame than the selection rects it compares them against
samples.evidence: Production code builds the box as `y: pageY + pl.y + pl.line.height - drawH` (doc-canvas.ts:604), but the test uses `y: pl.y + pl.line.height - drawH` (line 96) while `computeSelectionRects` returns rects that include the page Y offset (`getPageYOffset` = Theme.pageGap + ... , pagination.ts:194-200). The tests still pass only because the image height (80) exceeds the page gap so the bands accidentally still overlap. Consequently the vertical half of the intersection is not meaningfully asserted in the integration-style test, and any y-axis regression (or a multi-page case) would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The new bare-modifier passthrough is only covered for Meta/Control; the 'Shift' and 'Alt' arms are not distinguished by any assertion
samples.evidence: editor.ts returns false for key === 'Meta' | 'Control' | 'Shift' | 'Alt'. Only Meta/Control are pinned ('a bare modifier keydown does not clear the image selection', image-copy.test.ts:377-394). The Shift+X test (line 255) and Option+X test (line 284) dispatch the bare 'Shift'/'Alt' keydown, but their assertions (no clipboard payload, image still present) hold identically if those keys fall through to the catch-all and clear the image selection — neither test observes `editor.getSelectedImage()` afterwards. So the claim in the comment that holding Shift must not drop the image selection is untested; a regression would silently deselect the image while extending a selection.

verdict.reason: The new test never drives the fixed call site. `tintedIndicesFor` (image-selection-tint.test.ts:87-105) copies the DocCanvas render loop into the test and always constructs an unrounded box (`x: pageX + pl.x + run.x`, line 95), then calls `imageIntersectsSelection` directly; that helper (doc-canvas.ts:151-162) is a plain unconditional rectangle overlap test and cannot express the bug. The actual fix is at doc-canvas.ts:600-611, where the overlap must be measured on the unrounded box while only `fillRect(Math.round(box.x), Math.round(box.y), ...)` rounds — restoring `Math.round` in the box passed to `imageIntersectsSelection` would leave every assertion in the new file passing. I searched widely for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for `DocCanvas` shows no test ever constructs one; table-renderer.test.ts:653-675 is only a static import-symbol scan (no rounding/tint guard); image-selection-overlay.test.ts:28-73 records fillRect for the eight resize handles only; table-renderer.ts:424-447 has a parallel image-tint branch with no test at all; no `*.test.ts` in packages/ mentions the tint or `selectionColorInactive` besides this file; no collocated docs src tests and no docs e2e specs. So the changed behavior (a user-visible mis-tint of a neighbouring image) has no test that can fail if it regresses.
